title: Roman Abramovich buys Chelsea
detail: From Ken Bates. The club season page and Bates' article say July 2003; Abramovich's article says the deal was June 2003.
evidence: In July 2003, long-time chairman Ken Bates sold the club to Russian billionaire Roman Abramovich.

title: £140 million
detail: What Bates sold for, and his profit.
evidence: In 2003, he sold the club to Russian oil billionaire Roman Abramovich for a sum of £140 million, making a £17 million profit.

title: "Russian tanks on our lawn"
detail: Arsenal's vice-chairman on the new money (Arsenal's season page).
evidence: Arsenal vice-chairman David Dein however was displeased, and quipped that Abramovich had "parked his Russian tanks on our lawn and is firing £50 notes at us", Abramovich was said to have placed a bid for Arsenal striker Thierry Henry, which was turned down at once.

title: Damien Duff: £17m release clause
detail: Part of a summer in which Chelsea bought Duff, Verón, Crespo, Mutu, Makélélé, Joe Cole, Bridge, Geremi, Glen Johnson and Smertin (see transfers.csv).
evidence: In the run up to the 2003–04 season, Chelsea made a series of bids for Duff, with a £17 million offer, eventually triggering a release clause in the player's contract.

title: European football under the new owner
detail: Champions League third qualifying round, first leg: Žilina 0–2 Chelsea (date from the match data); Duff "the star of the show".
evidence: Signed by manager Claudio Ranieri as part of the development of Chelsea financed by new owner Roman Abramovich, Duff made his debut in August 2003 in the Champions League against Slovak side MŠK Žilina.

title: Verón scores on debut at Anfield
detail: Liverpool 1–2 Chelsea; injuries then limit him to 15 appearances.
evidence: Verón made an excellent start to his Chelsea career by scoring the opening goal in a 2–1 victory over Liverpool at Anfield, but he fell away with injury problems as the 2003–04 season progressed and made only 15 appearances for Chelsea.

title: London derby: Chelsea 4–2 Tottenham
detail: Premier League 5. For: Lampard 34'; Mutu 36'; Mutu 74'; Hasselbaink 90'; against: Kanouté 24'; Kanouté 86'

title: Lampard: Player of the Month
evidence: The following season, he was selected as the Premier League Player of the Month in September 2003, and the PFA Fans' Player of the Month in October.

title: Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea
detail: Premier League 9. For: Crespo 8'; against: Edu 5'; Henry 75'

title: Longest league winning run begins (5 wins)

"The Tinkerman"
detail: Ranieri rotates the expensive new squad.
evidence: During the 2002–03 season and throughout his Chelsea days, Ranieri was accused of over-rotating his squad, picking up the nickname of "The Tinkerman" from the British media.

title: Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea
detail: FA Cup Fifth round. For: Mutu 40'; against: Reyes 56'; Reyes 61'

title: Out of the FA Cup: Arsenal 2–1 Chelsea
Chelsea 1–2 Arsenal
detail: Premier League 26. For: Guðjohnsen 1'; against: Vieira 15'; Edu 21'

title: Chelsea 1–1 Arsenal
detail: Champions League Quarter-final, first leg. For: Guðjohnsen 53'; against: Pirès 59'

title: Bridge knocks Arsenal out at Highbury
detail: Champions League quarter-final, second leg, 88th minute: Chelsea into the semi-finals.
evidence: Bridge scored the winning goal in the 88th minute to send Chelsea into the semi-finals and end an 18-game winless run against Arsenal.

title: Arsenal 1–2 Chelsea
detail: Champions League Quarter-final, second leg. For: Lampard 51'; Bridge 87'; against: Reyes 46'

title: Out to Monaco in the semi-final
detail: 5–3 on aggregate; Ranieri blamed for his substitutions in the first leg.
evidence: The club also reached the semi-finals of the Champions League; Chelsea eliminated Arsenal en route, although Ranieri's position was weakened by the semi-final loss to Monaco, a result the manager himself was blamed for due to several bizarre substitutions and tactical changes.

title: Out of the Champions League: Chelsea 2–2 Monaco
Manchester United 1–1 Chelsea
detail: Premier League 37. For: Grønkjær 19'; against: Van Nistelrooy 77'

title: Runners-up, up from fourth
detail: The first season after the takeover.
evidence: Chelsea finished their first season after the takeover in second place in the Premier League, up from fourth the previous year.

title: Lampard second to Henry
detail: FWA Footballer of the Year runner-up; PFA Team of the Year; 10 league goals.
evidence: At the end of the season, he came second behind Thierry Henry for the 2004 FWA Footballer of the Year award.

title: Mourinho's Porto win the Champions League
detail: Against Monaco, the team that knocked Chelsea out.
evidence: Porto lost the 2004 Taça de Portugal Final to Benfica in May 2004, but two weeks later, Mourinho won a greater prize: the UEFA Champions League, with a 3–0 win over Monaco in Germany.

title: Ranieri sacked
detail: The season page says 31 May; Ranieri's article dates his tenure to 30 May 2004.
evidence: Manager Claudio Ranieri was sacked on 31 May 2004 and was replaced by José Mourinho for the following season.

title: Epilogue: Mourinho arrives
detail: The first Portuguese manager in the Premier League.
evidence: On 2 June 2004, Mourinho moved to Chelsea on a three-year contract, after a £1.7 million compensation package was agreed with Porto, making him the first Portuguese manager in the Premier League.
